https://atomicdata.dev/properties/descri: The plugin catalog for this repository's integrations: visibility flags and card copy per entry. The data-browser fetches this file at runtime from GitHub Pages (https://ontola.github.io/atomic-plugins/integrations/catalog.json by default, configurable in Settings > Integration), not from the connected server. At the pinned atomic-server it reads only `shortname`, `experimental`, `enabled` and `requires-api-plugins`, to decide whether to offer the 'Show experimental plugins' toggle; it renders no card from this file (see integrations/READINESS.md). Where `shortname` equals a package directory under integrations/ (money, notion, pets), the entry's `version` must equal that package's (integrations/README.md, 'Version and catalog entry'). Flip `experimental` to `false` once its package.json `atomicCertification.support` has left "experimental" — see integrations/README.md.
One integration's visibility gate and, for a bundled one, its card copy.

True until this integration's advertised capabilities have current live evidence. An experimental entry is hidden from the Integrations page unless the visitor turns on 'Show experimental plugins'. Only meaningful when `enabled` is true.
Whether this integration can be offered at all. False, same as omitting the entry entirely, means the Integrations page never offers it, even with 'Show experimental plugins' on.
What this bundled integration's sync or import can actually do, shown on its Integrations page card.
How and when this bundled integration exchanges data, shown on its Integrations page card.
The supported scope and caveats, shown in the card's 'Supported scope' details.
Extra space-separated search terms matched against the Integrations page search box, alongside name and description.

True if this integration's card was meant to appear only once a visitor also enabled 'Show API plugins'. atomic-server removed that toggle with the LocalThought flow (c707ca4ed); at the pin, entries with this flag are not offered and do not count towards showing the 'Show experimental plugins' toggle.
The LocalThought platform id this integration's setup dialog connects through, for one that uses the generic LocalThought extension flow instead of its own setup component.
The platform id LocalThought's OAuth callback reports back, for an integration that owns its own setup component instead of using the generic LocalThought flow (so it has no `platform`).

https://atomicdata.dev/properties/descri: Bring your Todoist projects and tasks into a local issue tracker.
https://atomicdata.dev/integrations/prop: Imports active tasks and projects. Tasks open in the Issues view with their title, due day and priority. Todoist lists active tasks only, so a task shows as closed only when Todoist itself reports it checked.
Connect through LocalThought, then Sync now (and every five minutes while the folder is open) to pull the latest tasks.

Read only: the proxy's Todoist access is data:read, so closing, editing or creating a task here is not sent to Todoist. A task that stops appearing is never assumed completed. The lens can check such a task by id and mark it completed, deleted, unavailable or unconfirmed, with when it was last seen, but no host runs that check yet, and nothing has been verified against a live Todoist account.
todoist tasks todo projects devonian lens local tracker issues
